patient_view_access_log_own_ceiling.description: A patient attempts to view another patient's access log while the request context names the other patient. This should not be permitted under the patient's own-access-log path.

personal_representative_view_represented.description: A personal representative with an active session tries to view the access log for a patient included in their representedPatients set; a policy that only permits patients to view their own logs would incorrectly deny this required workflow.
A personal representative tries to view an access log for a patient who is not in their representedPatients set, even though the session is active.

patient_view_own_medical_record_floor.description: A patient attempts to view another patient's medical record while using their own active session. The own-record equality should prevent treating Patient role membership alone as sufficient.

patient_view_own_medical_record_ceiling.description: A patient attempts to view another patient's medical record while using their own active session; the ownership boundary should prevent this over-permission.

personal_representative_view_represented.description: A personal representative attempts to view a medical record for a patient not in their representedPatients set; a broad role-only policy would incorrectly permit it.

lhcp_view_patient_allowed_diagnostic_inf.description: An LHCP who is explicitly listed in the diagnostic information's allowedViewers attempts to view that patient's diagnostic information using their own active session; a deny-only policy would incorrectly block this approved workflow.
An LHCP attempts to view diagnostic information for the patient named in the request, but the patient has not included that LHCP in the diagnostic information's allowed viewers.

patient_view_own_personal_health_informa.description: A patient attempts to view another patient's personal health information by setting the request context to the other patient; the ownership boundary should block this even though the principal is a Patient.

personal_representative_view_represented.description: A personal representative tries to view personal health information for a patient who is not in their representedPatients set, even though the session is active.

patient_view_own_family_history_ceiling.description: A patient attempts to view another patient's family-history record by setting the request patient context to the other patient. The ceiling rejects this broader access because both context.patient and resource.patient must equal the principal.

patient_view_own_immunization_ceiling.description: A patient attempts to view another patient's immunization record by supplying the other patient in the request context.

personal_representative_view_represented.description: A personal representative attempts to view a family-history record for a patient they do not represent, even though their session is active.
A personal representative tries to view an immunization record for a patient who is not in their representedPatients set, even though the session is active.
A personal representative attempts to view an office visit for a patient who is not in their representedPatients set, even though the session is active and belongs to them.

patient_take_own_untaken_office_visit_su.description: A patient attempts to take the survey for another patient's office visit; the ownership boundary should prevent this floor from requiring permission.
A patient attempts to take their own office-visit survey after it has already been taken; the survey lifecycle boundary should prevent this floor from requiring permission.
A patient attempts to take a survey for their own office visit after the survey has already been submitted. The ceiling should reject policies that permit this broader lifecycle case.
diagnostic_for: same-action ceiling for approved patient survey floor

patient_take_own_untaken_office_visit_su.description: A patient attempts to take a survey for another patient's office visit. The ceiling should reject policies that omit the own-record boundary.

personal_representative_take_represented.description: A personal representative tries to take a survey for an office visit belonging to a patient they do not represent, even though the session is active and the survey has not yet been taken.
A personal representative tries to take a survey for a represented patient's office visit after the survey has already been taken.

hcp_create_patient_ceiling.description: An HCP attempts to create a patient using an inactive session. The floor alone would not prevent a broader synthesized policy from allowing this mutable account creation, so the ceiling bounds it to active sessions.

hcp_disable_patient_floor.description: A candidate policy that never permits HCPs to disable patients would violate the explicit workflow even if it satisfies unrelated safety constraints.

administrator_assign_listed_hospital_flo.description: An administrator tries to assign an LHCP to a Hospital entity that is not included in the hospital list supplied in the request context; this should not satisfy the listed-hospital floor.

administrator_assign_listed_hospital_cei.description: An administrator with an active session attempts to assign an LHCP to a Hospital entity that is not a member of the provided hospital list; the ceiling should reject any candidate policy that permits this request.

patient_add_lhcp_to_own_provider_list_fl.description: A patient attempts to add an LHCP to another patient's provider list. The chosen floor does not require permission for that cross-patient request because the provider-list resource is not the requesting patient.

patient_designate_lhcp_for_self_ceiling.description: A patient attempts to designate an LHCP on a ProviderDesignation record whose patient is someone else; relying only on the Patient principal type would over-permit this cross-patient mutation.

hcp_edit_active_selected_patient_persona.description: An HCP attempts to edit personal health information for a selected patient whose Patient.isActive flag is false. The repaired floor should not require permission because deactivated patients cannot be modified.
An HCP attempts to edit personal health information for a different patient than the one selected in the request context; this should not be required by the floor even if both patients are active.
